p: who caused the entire world to rebel against Me during his reign
how many are the years of a person
“The days of our years are seventy years and with strength eighty years”
from the earth to the … firmament … is a walking
from the earth to the first firmament of seven (see Ḥagiga 12b) is a walking
and the thickness of the firmament is a walking
and so too between each and every firmament.
“Yet you shall be brought down to the netherworld,
to the uttermost parts of the pit”
The Jewish Sages say the celestial sphere
is stationary, … and the constellations revolve
and the sages of the nations of the world say the … celestial sphere revolves,
and the sages of the nations of the world say the entire celestial sphere revolves,
A refutation of their words … we have never found
A refutation of their words that the entire sphere moves can be derived from the fact that we have never found
Ursa Major in the South or Scorpio in the North.

p: Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov strongly objects to this
like the pivot of a door,
during the day the sun travels beneath the firmament
And the sages of the nations of the world say
during the day the sun travels beneath the firmament,
beneath the earth … Rabbi … said: … And the statement … appears … than our statement. … that during the day, … springs

beneath the earth and around to the other side of the world. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said: And the statement of the sages of the nations of the world appears to be more accurate than our statement. A proof to this is that during the day, springs
and during the night they are hot

w.31: beneath the earth … our statement … that during the … springs

p: During the summer the sun travels high in the sky,
therefore the entire world is hot,
during the winter the sun travels low in the sky,
The sun travels in four paths
travels over the mountains in order to melt the snows
the settlement in order to ripen the produce.
it travels over the seas in order to dry the rivers,
it travels over the desert in order to not dry the seeds
And even though he is able to enter
we do not say to him:
Get up and enter; … But wasn’t it taught … An
Get up and enter; rather, we rely on the fact that at the critical moment he is outside the courtyard. But wasn’t it taught in a baraita: An
uncircumcised Jew who did not circumcise

w.4: for one who is ritually pure

p: a distant journey is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb, … and … a distant journey is stated with regard to … tithe, … Just as later … outside … where it … be eaten,

a distant journey is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb, and the exemption of a distant journey is stated with regard to the second tithe, as the verse states: “And if the way be too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it because the place is too far from you, which the Lord your God shall choose to set His name there” (Deuteronomy 14:24). Just as later in the Torah, with regard to the second tithe, the exemption applies only to someone located outside the area where it may be eaten,

w.19: later … outside … where it … be eaten

p: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda says,
where the offering of the Paschal lamb may be performed,
is that which Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Rav Yosef said:
follow the majority of those standing in the courtyard,
Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda said, … citing Rabbi Eliezer,
Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda said, citing Rabbi Eliezer,
Rabbi Yosei said to him: … Therefore,
and is not on a journey”
it teaches that from the threshold of the courtyard and beyond is called a journey,
